title.narrative: Strengthening networking among CAFOD partners in Tanzania

description.narrative:
According to Tanzania HIV and AIDS and Malaria Indicator Survey 2007-2008, the national prevalence among the sexually active populations (between 15 and 49 years of age) is 5.7%. About 6.6% are women and 4.6% are men. It has made more than 2 million orphans which need assistance. More than 50% of beds occupants in many health facilities are occupied by infected people. The most affected are women and people living in rural areas. It has been difficulty for the rural people to access services such as ARVS and VCT.
Partners in this project include Dar-es-Salaam Archdiocese Health Education Programme (DACHEP), Archdiocese of Arusha Integrated Development and Relief Office (AAIDRO), Diocese of Mbulu Development Department (DMDD), Diocese of Moshi Rainbow Centre, Diocese of Same and Caritas Tanzania (CT). These partners are engaged in various development work aimed at supporting the communities through programmes related to HIV and AIDS, water supply and sanitation, food security, gender, microfinance, education and disaster management. These organizations will continue to inspire positive and sustainable changes in individuals and communities and enable them become accountable to the communities and partners as well as stakeholders.
This three year programme is build upon and informed by experiences and lessons learnt from year 2009 project called “Strengthening Networking among CAFOD Partners in Tanzania facilitated by CT”. Among others, participating partners learnt that they differed in terms of responses in managing community development programmes, knowledge and skills in designing programmes and competence in implementing the programmes. Additionally, most of the partners have good practices and experiences from their programme work that are inadequately documented and disseminated for wider learning.
To achieve the goal and objectives of this project, CT through the project will built the capacity of development officers through organizing training workshops and encouraging horizontal learning. Two training workshops will be organized one will be for enhancing monitoring and evaluation knowledge and skills and another will be on advocacy and lobbying. The workshops will involve development officers engaged in managing the programs. The project will facilitate and encourage the sharing of experience through organizing exposure and sharing of reports among member organizations.
CT will be the lead partner in the proposed project and will facilitate dialogue and exchange of experiences and ideas on matters related to development and social welfare activities among selected dioceses/partners. CT will work with the partners in linking them with other agencies and stakeholders and mobilizing resources from within and outside Tanzania for learning and to strengthen development work in respective organizations. CT will support partners in undertaking monitoring and evaluation, staff recruitment and provide capacity building services. During this period, this project will also carry out advocacy actions at national and international levels with support of the selected bishops.
